intended_object: The potential energy 𝒱(μ) = ∫ V dμ of a measure μ in a potential V, as an extended real number. When the positive part has infinite integral the value is +∞; otherwise it is ∫V⁺ − ∫V⁻, which may be −∞. This is the convention of Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré §9.3, and it is given in the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body checks whether ∫⁻ V⁺ dμ = ∞ and returns ⊤ in that case. Otherwise it returns (∫⁻ V⁺ : EReal) − (∫⁻ V⁻ : EReal), where V⁺ = ofReal V and V⁻ = ofReal (−V). This is exactly the integral of the positive part minus that of the negative part, extended to EReal with +∞ taking precedence. If only the negative part is infinite, finite − ⊤ = ⊥, as the docstring says. If both are infinite, the value is ⊤, which is the convention the docstring states.

For integrable V the value agrees with the Bochner integral (`potentialEnergy_of_integrable`). Using the Lebesgue integral `lintegral` also means non-measurable potentials get a sensible lower-integral value instead of a junk 0.

On generality: it works on any measurable space, for any measure, with a real-valued V. The literature sometimes allows V to take values in (−∞, +∞]. That is a minor restriction and does not change the nature of the construction. Mathlib has no EReal-valued integral of real functions with this ⊤-precedence convention, so there is no more general Mathlib counterpart.
